High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Applicant :- Rizwan Khan @ Arbaz Khan
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Manoj Kumar Misra,Manoj Kumar Singh,Nishit Upreti
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Bal Krishna Shukla
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Shri Bal Krishna Shukla, learned counsel for the informant has sent an illness slip which is
opposed by learned counsel for the applicant on the ground that the applicant is in custody since
26.06.2023 and this Court had directed that the statement of the victim be recorded within a period
of two months which has been recorded and it does not support the prosecution story, as such, the
matter should be heard.

2.  Considering the fact that the applicant is in custody since 26.06.2023 and the opposition of the applicant to the illness slip of counsel for the informant, I proceed to hear the matter with the assistance of learned AGA.
Rizwan Khan @ Arbaz Khan vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 3.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.161 of 2023, under Section 376(3), 376(DA),
504, 506, 507 IPC, Section 3/4(2), 5(g)/6 of POCSO Act, Section 3(2)V, 3(1)(da), 3(1)(dha) of SC/ST Act & Section 66(E) of Information Technology Act, P.S. Risia, District Bahraich.

4. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the informant was belonging to Scheduled Castes and around two years ago, the applicant used to frequently visit the home where he met the daughter of the informant and on the false pretext of marriage formed physical relations with her.

Subsequently,
allegations of blackmailing and threatening for conversion were also levelled.

5. In the light of the said, the submission of counsel for the applicant is that the informant admitted during her statement that the applicant used to visit the daughter of the informant around 4 to 6 months ago.
He also draws my attention to the statement of the victim herself wherein she admitted that the applicant became friendly to the victim and they used to talk on telephone.
She also admitted that after nine months of the initial friendship, she had disclosed to her mother that she was in love with the applicant and wanted to marry as proposed by the applicant.
6. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the two statements which have been recorded in terms of the directions given by this Court coupled with the allegations in the FIR that physical relations continued allegedly on the false pretext of marriage over a long span of time as well as the fact that there is no process adopted so far to conclusively determine the age of the victim, the applicant who is in custody since 26.06.2023 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Rizwan Khan @ Arbaz Khan be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.4.2024 nishant  Rizwan Khan @ Arbaz Khan vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...
